title: The Expressive Power of Constrained QAOA: What You Might Have MISsed
authors: Boris Tsvelikhovskiy, Bao Bach, Ilya Safro
abstract: Feasibility-preserving mixer Hamiltonians offer an attractive alternative to penalty encodings for constrained quantum optimization, yet how enforcing constraints alters the state space reachable by the Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA) remains largely unexplored. We address this question within the context of the Maximum Independent Set (MIS) problem. Alongside the standard controlled bit-flip mixer, we analyze the alternative $\mathit{Flip\text{-}or\text{-}Stay}$ mixer, whose restriction to the feasible subspace $W_{\mathcal{F}}$ corresponds precisely to the shifted negative Laplacian of the independent-set reconfiguration graph. Although both mixers induce identical transitions between independent sets, the diagonal modification changes the spectral structure and can substantially enlarge the set of reachable quantum states.   For every connected input graph with at least two vertices, we prove that independently parameterized local controls associated with either mixer generate the full unitary Lie algebra on the feasible subspace. Standard QAOA exhibits a more nuanced algebraic structure. We prove that the dynamical Lie algebra associated with MIS-QAOA employing the conventional mixer embeds into its Flip-or-Stay counterpart. Furthermore, we construct an infinite family of graphs for which the corresponding vacuum-state dynamical group orbits exhibit strictly distinct dimensions, establishing a qualitative expressivity separation between the two architectures. For either mixer, we show that standard QAOA initialized in the empty set can prepare a state supported entirely on maximum independent sets at finite depth. For the free architectures, we also derive an exact loss-variance formula in the unitary-design limit, expressed through the number of feasible independent sets and the variance of their cardinalities.
summary: This work rigorously compares two types of mixers used in constrained QAOA for solving MIS. It proves that the alternative 'Flip-or-Stay' mixer offers superior expressive power compared to the standard mixer, demonstrating a qualitative gap in the reachable quantum states. The findings are crucial for understanding the fundamental limitations and potential enhancements in quantum optimization algorithms.
main_problem: The paper investigates the expressive power and controllability of constrained quantum optimization algorithms, specifically for the Maximum Independent Set (MIS) problem.
main_result: It establishes a qualitative expressivity separation between two mixer types (standard vs. Flip-or-Stay) and proves that for connected graphs, the free mixer generates the full unitary Lie algebra on the feasible subspace.
method: The analysis relies heavily on comparing the dynamical Lie algebras generated by different mixer Hamiltonians (standard vs. alternative) when restricted to the feasible subspace defined by independent sets.
model_or_system: The model is constrained quantum optimization dynamics applied to the MIS problem on a graph $\Gamma$. The dynamics are governed by mixers, such as the standard controlled bit-flip mixer and the alternative Flip-or-Stay mixer, acting within the feasible subspace $\mathcal{W}_F$.
key_observables: Controllability (generating the full unitary Lie algebra), expressivity separation (comparing orbit dimensions), and the variance of the loss function in the unitary-design limit.
important_parameters: The graph structure ($\Gamma$), the depth of the QAOA circuit ($p$), and the dimensionality of the feasible subspace ($|F|$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the circuit ensemble forms an exact unitary 2-design for variance calculations, and it focuses on the operator-algebraic structure rather than just approximation quality.
paper_structure: The paper proceeds by defining the constrained dynamics for MIS, comparing the algebraic structures of the standard and alternative mixers, proving full controllability for the free architecture, and finally establishing the expressivity gap using graph families.
why_interesting: The detailed algebraic comparison of different quantum control Hamiltonians (Laplacian vs. Adjacency) provides deep insight into which physical constraints yield the most powerful quantum computational models.
